testRigor provides several built-in reusable rules for common actions such as logging in, signing up, logging out, and selecting dates. These rules simplify test creation by handling common workflows without requiring you to write every individual step.


In this article, we’ll cover the following built-in rules:


1. ` login` – Log into an application using configured or stored credentials.
2. ` sign up` – Register a new account with automatically generated credentials.
3. ` logout` – Sign out of an application.
4. ` pick` – Select individual dates or date ranges.


## Login


The built-in` login` rule automatically logs into your application using the credentials configured under **Settings → Authentication → App-specific Authentication** .


```text
login
```


Alternatively, you can define the stored values` username` and` password` in your Test Data to override the default authentication credentials.


You can also explicitly specify which stored values to use:


```text
login with stored value "newEmail" and stored value "newPassword"
```


Unlike the signup rule, the login rule does not generate new credentials. It uses the credentials provided to it.


You can also override the default credentials by assigning new values to` username` and` password` :


```text
save " [email protected]  " as "username"
save "SecurePassword123!" as "password"
login
```


Or provide the credentials directly:


```text
login with username " [email protected]  " and password "SecurePassword123!"
```


## Signup


The built-in` sign up` rule automatically generates and saves the following stored values during registration:


**Note:** The rule first looks for a sign-up button to click, so make sure you’re on a page where the sign-up option is available.


```text
generate unique email and save it as "newEmail"
generate by regex "[a-z0-9]{18}!" and save it as "newPassword"
save "James" as "user_name"
save "Gatsby" as "user_last_name"
```


These stored values are generated or assigned when the` sign up` rule executes. Any existing values with the same names will be overwritten.


## Reusing Signup Credentials


Once registration is complete, you can reuse the generated credentials in subsequent test steps:


```text
sign up
enter stored value "newEmail" into "Email"
enter stored value "newPassword" into "Password"
click "Sign In"
```


Alternatively, you can pass these stored values directly to the built-in` login` rule:


```text
sign up
login with stored value "newEmail" and stored value "newPassword"
```


## Logout


The built-in` logout` rule automatically looks for a logout button and clicks it to sign out of the application.


```text
login with stored value "newEmail" and stored value "newPassword"
logout
```


## Dates


testRigor also provides built-in rules for selecting individual dates and date ranges.


```text
pick "mm/dd/yyyy" from "element"
```


```text
pick dates from "mm/dd/yyyy" to "mm/dd/yyyy"
```
